newsitem.title: UK: Boeing sees Europe-N.America cargo 7pc growth.
newsitem.headline: Boeing sees Europe-N.America cargo 7pc growth.

text.p: Two-way air cargo traffic between Europe and North America is expected to grow at an average annual rate of seven percent between now and 2015, Boeing Co said.
In its latest World Air Cargo Forecast published here on Thursday it said eastbound traffic is expected to grow at 6.7 percent annual average rate, and westbound by 7.2 percent.

Some 3.60 million tonnes would be carried eastbound to Europe in 2015 on the basis of this estimate, compared to 986,000 tonnes in 1995, while westbound tonnages would then reach 3.84 million, against 952,000 tonnes last year.
Boeing said the overall market "has exhibited some weakness, causing concern in 1996". This follows a rise of almost 18 percent in 1994, which then slowed to 5.3 percent last year
"Real yield for 1995 was up almost six percent with excess freighter capacity vanishing," it added.
The UK and Germany regularly provide almost half of the two-way trade, with five countries accounting for three-quarters of total tonnage in 1995, it said.
There were the UK with 22.3 percent, Germany 21.5 percent, France (12.4 percent), Italy (10.3 percent) and the Netherlands (8.7 percent).

As "airfreight volume is proportional to economic activity, the GDPs of Europe and North America are prime generators of growth in the North Atlantic market. Directionality of traffic is highly sensitive to exchange rate," Boeing said.
"Future impacts can only be speculated. Therefore, the current forecast does not assume an appreciable change in U.S.-Europe exchange rates over the long term."
